summary.one_liner: DeepTutor is an open-source, agent-based AI learning workspace that combines tutoring, chat, quizzes, deep research, visualization, and mastery practice with a knowledge base and persistent memory.
keywords: open source alternative to ai tutors
summary.what_it_does: DeepTutor is a learning workspace in which chat, Ask Questions, quiz generation, deep research, visualization, problem solving, mastery paths, immersive reading, and audio overviews share one agent runtime and session context. It supports knowledge bases built with several retrieval engines (LlamaIndex, PageIndex, GraphRAG, LightRAG, and others) with pluggable document parsing. Users can attach books, notebook pages, question banks, and memory to workflows, and the memory system is layered and editable. It also provides a Task Board for study tasks, YouTube and Bilibili video reading with transcript search, and the ability to consult external agent harnesses or custom "Partners" from chat. Installation options include a PyPI package with a web app and CLI, a source checkout, a Docker container, and a CLI-only mode.
use_cases: Study from my own textbooks and PDFs with an AI tutor
Generate quizzes and practice questions from course material
Run deep research on a topic and get a report
Build a personal knowledge base and chat with it
Create visual explanations or short video lessons
Self-host a private AI tutoring web app
notable: Single runtime shared by many modes (chat, quiz, research, visualize, solve, mastery path, reading)
Multiple interchangeable RAG engines per knowledge base, including a self-hosted LightRAG Server and WeKnora
Layered, inspectable memory (L1 traces, L2 summaries, L3 synthesis) with a memory graph
Consult live external agent harnesses (e.g., Claude Code, Codex) or custom Partners from chat
Sandboxed code execution for office-file skills (docx/pdf/pptx/xlsx)
caveats: Large, fast-moving project: many releases per month, and the README describes frequent breaking changes (e.g., v1.6.3 front/back-end refactor, v1.7.0 modular install where feature modules must match the core version)
Full app needs Python plus Node.js runtimes; some features need extra installs (FFmpeg for certain speech adapters, LaTeX/ffmpeg for Math Animator, libolm for Matrix E2EE)
Model features require configuring your own LLM/embedding provider keys; Windows and Docker networking need extra setup for local model servers
